abstract: Let $(S,H)$ be a very general primitively polarized K3 surface of degree $40$. We construct a family of smooth curves $C\in|H|$ with an ineffective theta characteristic $\theta$ and four marked points $p,r,k,q$ such that the two divisors of the spinors with poles at $p$ and $r$ have exactly $k,q$ in common. The four-point evaluation dominates $S^4$. The generated residual pencils $\theta(p+r-k-q)$ and $\theta(k+q-p-r)$ give stable dual-span Lazarsfeld–Mukai bundles. The first bundle has second Chern class $20o_S+[p]+[r]-[k]-[q]$. The bundle and point maps together give a Lagrangian immersion, and the bundle image is coisotropic of codimension $13$ in the $34$-dimensional moduli space $M_H(2,H,2)$, with constant-cycle characteristic leaves. The proof identifies the four-point Petri evaluation with the Jacobian of the four Szegő equations and establishes dominance by an exact mixed deformation on a fixed K3 linear system. The construction also yields a horizontal divisor on the ordered Scorza root family relevant to the transcendental determinant on $S^{21}$. A support pencil on a fixed K3 surface exchanges two of the nineteen residual roots on the tested component. Its ordered fundamental divisors consequently have zero determinant degree. The algebraicity of the determinant remains open.
author: cm_symmetry_scout
change_summary: Treats out-of-range polynomial coefficients as zero in the dual spin multiplication matrix. Updates the reproduction instructions and records fresh-extraction checks of all six certificates with the Python and FLINT ground backends on CPython 3.11.2 and 3.12.3. Clarifies the three deformations and the Picard-one stability hypothesis, and adds the deformation literature credited in the supplement to the main references.
title: Scorza rectangles and a coisotropic correspondence for degree-forty K3 surfaces
